title: Procedural by-law, election resources and accessibility standards
subtitle: Council conference funding for double-hatted members, late meetings, investment returns and the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee's future.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended a new Regional Procedural By-law, with public notice to be given ahead of a planned Council vote on April 22, 2026 {{vote:m2}}. The changes are largely housekeeping, such as delegation rules for late-added reports and a fixed deadline for councillor notices of motion. Councillors also raised start times, the 11 p.m. extension rule and late agenda items, and staff will bring back options.

The committee also recommended adopting an updated policy on the use of corporate resources during an election {{vote:m3}}. Staff said Council needs to approve it before May 1 for it to apply to the coming municipal election. It covers all candidates, staff and third parties. On conferences, the committee directed staff to consult area municipalities and report back by August on fair access to funding for members who sit on two councils {{vote:m4}}.

The committee recommended asking the Province to build the latest Canadian Standards Association accessibility standards into the Building Code for new public buildings {{vote:m5}}. It also received the 2025 Accessibility Status Report and an investment position report, and asked for a report on the future of the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council give public notice of its intent to repeal the current procedural by-law and enact a new one effective April 23, 2026, with a Council vote planned for April 22.

decisions.item: Use of corporate resources during an election
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the updated policy, which applies to all candidates, regional staff, registered third parties and, where appropriate, members of the public.
The committee directed staff to consult area municipal staff and report back by the August 2026 committee cycle on equitable conference and development funding for double direct elected officials.

decisions.item: Accessibility standards in the Building Code
decisions.detail: The committee recommended asking the Province to adopt the latest CSA accessibility standards for new public buildings and to pursue Rick Hansen Foundation gold certification for its new buildings, with the motion sent to provincial and municipal bodies.

debate: On the procedural by-law, one councillor proposed moving the Council extension point from 11 p.m. to 10 p.m. Supporters said late-night decisions are poorer and unfair to staff. Others wanted data on how often meetings run past that time, and noted that delegations may be waiting. The amendment was withdrawn so staff could bring back options.

Councillors raised starting Council meetings earlier than 7 p.m. One said an earlier start could make it harder for working residents to attend as delegates. Others said committee days run late and clash with township council meetings, and suggested a different committee day.

Several councillors said too many reports are added through the late-starter addendum agenda, leaving the public and Council little time to review them. Staff said they would raise it with the leadership team.

On conferences, one councillor asked why the policy was being reviewed, given that it was created after a past double-billing case, and suggested township mayors be allowed to register as mayors. Township representatives said the current rules create a double standard and that costs could be split fairly. Staff said no registrations would change before August.

On the accessibility motion, a councillor asked whether it would raise housing costs. Staff said it covers public buildings only, so the operative wording was amended by unanimous consent to say new construction of public buildings. One councillor noted that ramps do not suit everyone and elevators and stairs are also needed. Members also said the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee should stay unified, and asked for a report on its future format.
